title: English TOEIC — vocabulaire et grammaire (tes notes)
src: Tes notes TOEIC / ETS / BTL1, questions de Claude
summary: Les mots que tu n'avais pas compris dans les textes ETS, les temps et pièges de grammaire de tes notes TOEIC, et le vocabulaire utile pour BTL1 (look up, clue, break down). À refaire 5 minutes par jour : les erreurs reviennent le lendemain.
points: Proceeds (pl.) = produit d'une vente ; owe = devoir ; raise = augmenter / lever / cultiver / élever
Méthode TOEIC: test blanc chronométré 2 h, puis 4 à 5 h de correction

mcq.q: 'Proceeds' (plural) from a concert means…
o: the money gained from the sale
mcq.why: Proceeds = profits from a sale. 'Proceed' (verb) means to continue. Ex: The proceeds will go to local charities.

mcq.q: 'I owe you a favor.' What does 'owe' mean?
o: to have a debt to someone
mcq.why: Owe = have a debt (FR: devoir). Debt = money you owe. 'Owed' as a participle: any taxes owed.

mcq.q: A 'grocer' is…
o: someone who runs a store selling food
mcq.why: Grocer = épicier.

mcq.q: 'The manager is going to raise my salary.' Here 'raise' means…
mcq.why: Raise has many meanings: move higher, make bigger/increase, grow a crop, keep animals, bring up children.

mcq.q: 'He raises cows and chickens.' Here 'raise' means…
mcq.why: Raise also = keep animals, or grow a crop (FR: cultiver).

mcq.q: 'Our company is leading in computer technology.' 'Lead' (v) means…
mcq.why: Lead (v) = be in front. Lead (n) can also mean the pencil metal (plomb) or a position ahead.

mcq.q: 'Can't afford' means…
o: not have enough money or time for something
mcq.why: Afford is usually used with can / can't. Ex: I need a vacation, but I can't afford the time.

mcq.q: 'The crowd cheered when their team scored.' 'Cheer' means…
mcq.why: Cheer = shout encouragement or approval.

mcq.q: What is a 'fund'?
o: a supply of money for a certain purpose
mcq.why: Ex: We intend to set up a fund to help music students pay for lessons.

mcq.q: 'Everyone got up when the bride entered.' 'Got up' means…
mcq.why: Get up = leave the bed, or stand up. A bride is a woman on her wedding day (FR: mariée).

mcq.q: 'I would like to withdraw some money.' 'Withdraw' means…
o: take money out of an account
mcq.why: Withdrawals = retraits. Cash deposits = dépôts. Takeaways and takeouts are for food.

mcq.q: 'This desk is for cash deposits only; ______ are over there.'
mcq.why: Takeouts/takeaways are food to eat at home; giveaways = free things; withdrawals = taking money out.

mcq.q: 'Our company needs money; it is looking out for new ______.'
mcq.why: The suffix -or/-er means the people who. Looking for people who invest = investors.

mcq.q: 'I ______ a report since 9 o'clock this morning.'
mcq.why: 'Since 9 o'clock' needs present perfect (continuous): started in the past, continues now.

mcq.q: Which tense: 'By 10 PM, we ______ the project.'
mcq.why: Future perfect: action completed before a specific time in the future.

mcq.q: Which tense: 'They ______ a movie when I called them.'
mcq.why: Past continuous: action in progress at a specific time in the past.

mcq.q: 'She ______ her homework before she went to bed.'
mcq.why: Past perfect: completed before another action in the past.

mcq.q: 'By 5 PM tomorrow, I ______ for 2 hours.'
mcq.why: Future perfect continuous: focus on the duration up to a future time.

mcq.q: 'He ______ basketball for 2 hours when he got injured.'
mcq.why: Past perfect continuous: duration up to another point in the past.

mcq.q: Which is gentler: 'have someone do something' or 'make someone do something'?
mcq.why: 'Make' is more like forcing someone.

mcq.q: 'cut down on something' means…
mcq.why: Phrasal verb: cut down on = reduce.

mcq.q: 'The experts recommend that the company ______ its investments.'
mcq.why: After recommend / suggest / advise + that, use the subjunctive, which looks like the infinitive.

mcq.q: '___ the substantial ______' : 'experts warn of a possibility of substantial ______.'
mcq.why: After the adjective 'substantial' a noun is needed: loss.

mcq.q: 'Videoconferencing is a popular tool ______ international businesses.'
mcq.why: Within = inside. Beneath = under. Into = with verbs of movement. Henceforth = from now on.

mcq.q: 'He is looking forward ______ his new job.'
mcq.why: Look forward to + gerund (-ing).

mcq.q: 'Contrary' is generally followed by…
mcq.why: Contrary to … ; and for currencies rising or falling we use 'against'.

mcq.q: 'All we could afford was a ______ car.'
mcq.why: Secondhand = used.

mcq.q: 'Money laundering' means…
o: illegally transferring money to hide its criminal origin
mcq.why: Laundering = hiding the original source.

mcq.q: 'If the service is good you should leave a ______.'
mcq.why: A tip = extra money given to someone who provided a service.

mcq.q: 'Take off' is used in…
o: 'Take off your jacket' and 'The airplane took off on time'
mcq.why: Take off has several meanings: remove, and leave the ground.

mcq.q: A 'grant' is…
o: money given by the government (for research, for example)
mcq.why: Ex: The research department registered 20 new patents.

mcq.q: 'Patents' fits: 'they have registered 20 new ______ this year.' Why not 'research'?
o: We need a countable noun after 20
mcq.why: Research is uncountable, so it cannot follow a number.

mcq.q: 'Postpone' means…
o: delay an event and plan it for a later date
mcq.why: Ex: We've had to postpone going to France because the children are ill.

mcq.q: 'Expedite' means…
mcq.why: Ex: if you want to expedite the process, update your logo.

mcq.q: 'Exhausted' is…
mcq.why: I'm feeling exhausted.

mcq.q: 'Flight attendant' in French is…
mcq.why: Attendant = someone whose job is to be in a place and help visitors or customers.

mcq.q: 'Sound' used as a verb, as in 'How does that sound to you?', means…
mcq.why: Sound good / interesting / strange = seem.

mcq.q: 'Pamphlet' is a synonym of…
mcq.why: A thin book with a few pages giving information or an opinion.

mcq.q: 'Vacant' means…
mcq.why: Ex: a vacant seat or position.

mcq.q: 'Intrigued' means…
mcq.why: Intrigued = very interested.

mcq.q: 'Account for' means…
mcq.why: Account for = explain the reason of something.

mcq.q: 'Delay' as a verb is a synonym of…
mcq.why: Delay = put off = postpone.

mcq.q: In the BTL1 notes: 'Look up' means…
o: search for a piece of information in a book or on the Internet
mcq.why: Useful for analysts: look up a hash or an IP.

mcq.q: In the BTL1 notes: 'Clue' means…
o: information that helps solve a crime or a problem
mcq.why: 'Not have a clue' = to not know or understand.

mcq.q: 'Break (something) down' means…
mcq.why: Break down can also mean stops working.

mcq.q: CFO, CMO, CHRO stand for…
o: Chief Financial / Marketing / Human Resources Officer
mcq.why: Also CPO (Production) and CCO (Customer).
